external_resources: Joseph Langer emigrated to the United States. He sailed alone from Antwerp aboard the S.S. Belgenland on 23 August 1923 and landed at Ellis Island on 2 September, aged 28, recorded as a merchant, last residence Nawsie, naming a cousin — Samuel Samul of Brzostek — as his nearest relative at home. He declared his intention in Brooklyn on 2 October 1923, petitioned for naturalisation on 9 January 1929, and was naturalised that year. Rose and their two children followed in 1929, six years after him: Harry, born in Brzostek on 11 November 1920, and Anna, born 22 December 1921 — both after this birth register closes in 1917. The United States census of April 1930 records the household in Brooklyn: Joseph, 34, salesman in a fruit store; Rose, 33; Harry, 8; and Florence, 7, who is Anna. In April 1942 he registered for the draft at 1418 East 4th Street, Brooklyn, aged 47, giving his birthplace as Brzostek.

external_resources: Rosa Langer née Rothman emigrated to the United States in 1929, six years after her husband, bringing their two children: Harry, born in Brzostek on 11 November 1920, and Anna, born 22 December 1921 — both after this birth register closes in 1917. Joseph Langer had sailed alone in 1923 and sent for them the year he was naturalised. The United States census of April 1930 records her in Brooklyn, aged 33 and still an alien, with Joseph, Harry (8) and Anna, entered as Florence (7). She was living at 1418 East 4th Street, Brooklyn, when Joseph registered for the draft in April 1942. Harry is named for Joseph's father, Hersch Langer, who died in Brzostek on 9 January 1908.
